articles.title: Cowboys Need A Massive Bounce Back In Green Bay
articles.summary: After a Thursday night loss to Tampa Bay, the Dallas Cowboys face a tough test at Lambeau Field. Can the team recover before their next primetime game?
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are reeling. That Thursday night loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers was a total disaster. Seeing the team fall 24-16 at home was hard to watch. Now, the squad has to find a way to recover before they head to Lambeau Field for Week 6.

The schedule isn't getting any easier. The Cowboys will travel to play the Green Bay Packers on Sunday, October 18. That game kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. It is the second of three straight primetime games for the team. I don't like the look of this stretch. You can't keep playing on national TV and losing like that.

The trip to Wisconsin is going to be brutal. The Cowboys are looking for a win to get back into the win column. It is hard to feel good about the team right now. Even the experts are skeptical. Per Sports Illustrated, it is tough to believe any oddsmakers would back the 'Boys after that last performance.

The pressure is mounting. The team needs to show progress. If they can't win in Green Bay, the season might start sliding. The defense has to step up. We saw what happened against Tampa Bay. We can't let it happen again in a cold stadium.

If you are a Bucs fan, you have a reason to smile. The Bucs are resting after their big win. Bucs fans should watch the Saints and Vikings game. A Saints loss would tie them at 1-4 in the division. That would be a huge win for Tampa Bay's standings.

There is also plenty to scout for the future. The Steelers and Colts both sit at 2-2. Since the Bucs face the Steelers next Sunday, this game is a great chance to see what's coming. The Cowboys face the Packers on Sunday, October 18, and the eyes of the league will be on them.

This accomplishment is a big step in Brown's fast-growing career. Earning a PGA Tour card is a major goal for golfers because it lets them compete with some of the world's best on the sport's top stage.

articles.title: As US suspends Green card programme for Infosys, TCS, Wipro and HCL; Shark Tank India judge Anupam Mittal remembers 'Full Emotional Atyachar' he faced when he went to return his Green Card years ago
articles.summary: As the US suspends a key green card step for several major Indian IT firms, entrepreneur and Shark Tank India judge and Shaadi.com founder Anupam Mittal
articles.body: As the US suspends a key green card step for several major Indian IT firms, entrepreneur and Shark Tank India judge and Shaadi.com founder Anupam Mittal has shared how he gave up his own green card, and why he sees America's immigration turmoil as an opportunity for India. Recently, the US government suspended several major technology and outsourcing firms, including Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL Technologies, Cognizant and Capgemini, from the Permanent Labor Certification Programme (PERM), a key route used by employers to sponsor foreign workers for employment-based green cards. The action also affects Microsoft and Adobe, with US authorities stating that they will neither accept new applications nor process pending labour certification requests involving the companies.The move has raised concerns among thousands of foreign workers, particularly Indians employed in the US technology sector. While the suspension does not affect existing H-1B visas, it could delay or block one of the most important pathways to permanent residency in the United States.Anupam Mittal recalls his own Green Card dilemmaIn a post shared on professional networking platform LinkedIn, Mittal shared a personal story about giving up his own Green Card years ago. Mittal said that, like many ambitious young Indians, he had once dreamed of building a life in America. He said he achieved that goal through a strong education, a successful job and financial success, becoming a multimillionaire within a few years."Within four years, I was a multimillionaire living the American dream. Then came the Green Card. I was ecstatic. But somehow the feeling was fleeting," he wrote. Mittal said that despite receiving permanent residency, he decided to move back to India in 2004 to build companies. However, he continued travelling to the US every year to maintain his residency status, even as he struggled with whether he should hold on to the Green Card.'The officer looked at me like I was crazy'The entrepreneur recounted visiting the US consulate in Mumbai to surrender the document. According to Mittal, the consular officer was surprised by his decision and urged him to reconsider."The officer looked at me like I was crazy. 'Think about this. Once you give it up, you may never get it back'," Mittal wrote. He jokingly described the exchange as "full emotional atyachar", adding that he ultimately walked out of the office with the Green Card still in his pocket.A year later, however, he returned and completed the process. "This time, I handed it over. And I walked out feeling lighter than I had in years. For the first time, both my feet were on the same side," he said.Mittal used the story to reflect on changing attitudes among Indian entrepreneurs and professionals. He said that had he remained in the United States, he might have become a wealthy technology executive. Instead, returning to India allowed him to build companies, invest in more than 300 startups and become part of the country's growing startup ecosystem.Read Anupam Mittal’s complete post hereLike most ambitious Indian kids, I dreamt of life in America.And I got there! articles.title: Golf: DP World Tour to refuse LIV players in 2027 season
articles.summary: The DP World Tour will not allow LIV Golf players to compete at its events in the 2027 season.
articles.body:
Players who sign up to LIV Golf next season will not be allowed to be members of the European tour in 2027.

The European tour, which is sponsored by DP World, said players must "make a choice" regarding where they play - a significantly tougher stance than in recent seasons.

Only players who are members of the DP World Tour can play for Europe in the Ryder Cup.

Deadlines for both tours are in the next five weeks, though there remains uncertainty surrounding LIV Golf's future despite it securing a possible $300m in funding as it attempts to restructure.

"Players need to make a choice," Guy Kinnings, CEO of the DP World Tour, told BBC Sport.

"We have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by.

"Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour."

In previous years, conditional releases were struck with some top players - including Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton - enabling them to play on both the DP World Tour and LIV.

However, players will be asked to disclose which tours they intend to play on for next year, and their answer will be taken into account when deciding on their membership.

Rahm to leave LIV Golf over 'unacceptable' terms

Strained smiles and uncertainty - the strange end of LIV Golf 1.0

About 15 LIV players - including Rahm, Hatton, Victor Perez and Tom McKibbin - have "status" with the DP World Tour, meaning they have eligibility under one of the membership categories.

Other LIV players, like Joaquin Niemann and Thomas Pieters, do not have such status so would either need to go through qualifying school or sign agreements with the DP World Tour by which they would receive invitations to a set number of tournaments.

However, those agreements would only be available to players who were not part of LIV in the future.

BBC Sport has been told the DP World Tour will not accept membership from anyone intending to play on what is being called LIV 2.0.

If players did not disclose their intention to play LIV and went on to do so, that would be considered grounds on which to have their membership terminated.

LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September as it attempted to restructure, following the withdrawal of its multi-billion dollar funding from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund.

Last week, it announced it had secured a possible $300m in financing from BC Partners Credit in order to try to move forward with the 2027 season.

LIV equity offer changes DP World Tour's approach

While the DP World Tour agreed to grant conditional releases with nine players this season, it is understood the change for 2027 is predominantly down to LIV offering players equity in future and a feeling this is incompatible with the European tour being a members organisation.

However, it also comes at a time when the DP World Tour's strategic alliance with the PGA Tour is being negotiated, so the move likely reflects a desire to put itself in the best position possible in those discussions.

Players will have until 16 November to sign up to the DP World Tour for next year.

Under the terms of its court-supervised restructuring process, LIV Golf needs to sign players up by 25 October.

Ted Goldthorpe, head of BC Partners Credit, told BBC Sport last week he was "confident" LIV would have a "critical mass" of players.

But since then two-time major winner Rahm has said he will not continue playing on the LIV tour.

Lawyers representing a number of other players, including fellow major winners Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith, sought clarification from the court that rejection of contracts would equate to "termination", enabling players to hold discussions with third parties about their futures.

Richard Bland is currently the only player to have stated publicly a desire to play on LIV 2.0.

However, Perez indicated last month he hoped there would be a future for the league.

articles.title: DP World Tour to deny LIV Golf players memberships for 2027 season - players must now 'make a choice'
articles.summary: The DP World Tour has said it will deny LIV Golf players memberships if they take part in the league for 2027; players need to be on the DP World Tour to be eligible for the Ryder Cup; players must now "make a choice"
articles.body:
Some of the world's top players were given conditional releases by the European tour in previous seasons, allowing them to compete on both circuits.

But DP World Tour chief executive officer Guy Kinnings has said players must now "make a choice".

In order to be eligible for Europe's Ryder Cup team, players must be members of the DP World Tour.

Kinnings told BBC Sport : "Players need to make a choice. We have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by.

"Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour."

LIV Golf chief executive Scott O'Neil has previously insisted that "one group of golfers" should not be "restricted from playing elsewhere".

LIV's future is in doubt after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew support at the end of the season and is going through Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the United States.

The breakaway series has secured an initial funding commitment for a potential $300m (£227m) investment from BC Partners Credit to help relaunch LIV 2.0 in 2027.

Deadlines for both tours fall next month and players will be asked to disclose which they intend to play on.

LIV players such as Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Victor Perez and Tom McKibbin are currently eligible to play on the DP World Tour under one of its membership categories.

Rahm is set to quit LIV Golf after refusing to accept new terms offered for its proposed relaunch and is reported to be owed up to $150m (£113m) for the remainder of the contract he signed almost three years ago.

articles.title: The Iran war didn't make your heating bill this high. Blue-state energy policy did
articles.summary: Blocked pipelines and refinery shortages explain why energy prices spike every winter, leaving families vulnerable to global oil market swings.
articles.body: Heating season is here, and the Iran war is getting the blame for higher energy prices. The war explains the timing. It doesn't explain the vulnerability. America produces enormous amounts of oil and gas. Why do prices jump when the Persian Gulf flares? Because oil trades on a world market. A crisis anywhere moves prices everywhere. But the real problem is policies at the state level that have kept us from truly unleashing the bounty of our domestic energy supply. CHEVRON CEO WARNS IRAN CONFLICT HAS CREATED 'VERY REAL' THREAT TO GLOBAL OIL SUPPLIES AS GAS PRICES CLIMB It’s been well documented that we have a refinery shortage. The country has 130 operable refineries, down from 301 in 1982, and no major new refinery has been built in the U.S. since 1976. Here in the Northeast, when we lost the Philadelphia Energy Solutions plant, we lost about 335,000 barrels a day. In my home state of New York, like so many other states, we also have a self-imposed supply problem. Natural gas moves through pipelines, and New York has blocked those pipelines. Pennsylvania, right next door, sits on some of the richest gas fields in the country. The Constitution Pipeline, if constructed, would carry that natural gas 124 miles, with 99 miles of new right-of-way in New York. AMERICAN BUSINESSES AREN’T ALLOWED TO BUILD. IT’S TIME CONGRESS HELPED THEM The fight to build this much-needed pipeline is now 10 years old. In April 2016, the state denied the water permit. Courts upheld it. The company tried again in 2025, then withdrew in November after three notices that its application was incomplete. And the problem runs deeper than one pipeline. Ill-conceived climate laws set sweeping emissions targets, and the plan to reach them is thin if not unattainable. Take New York City's Local Law 97. It fines large buildings that exceed emissions limits, and the limits tighten sharply in 2030. Owners must pay for costly retrofits or pay penalties. Either way, the bill lands on tenants, co-op owners and small businesses. THE REAL REASON YOUR ELECTRIC BILL IS SOARING THIS SUMMER WILL SURPRISE YOU Democrats in too many state capitals seem determined to choke off other reliable and cost-effective energy sources. Nuclear reactors and coal plants have closed down, both of which supply much-needed energy to citizens, especially low-income families. Meanwhile, the utility bills keep climbing, filling your gas tank becomes more painful, and truckers and shippers face punishing prices for diesel, which, of course, trickles down to raise the cost of everything from lumber to lunch meat. SENATORS PRESS PRESIDENT TRUMP TO RELEASE HOME HEATING OIL RESERVES AMID SOARING PRICES I’ve spent over 20 years in the energy and utility industry. Energy is not abstract. It is pipe, wire, steel and supply. Limit supply while demand holds, and prices rise. That is arithmetic, not ideology. And winter makes it more brutal. On the coldest days, when pipes run full, utilities scramble for alternatives and alternatives cost more. Families on fixed incomes can't opt out. They lower the thermostat and pull on another sweater. TRUMP ADMIN MOVES TO GUT BIDEN'S SIGNATURE ENVIRONMENTAL RULES Here is what should bother everyone, whatever their politics. A state that won't produce or import its own fuel doesn't become independent. It becomes a customer. It bids against the world for supply and accepts whatever price is asked, including prices set by wars it can't influence. The fight to build this much-needed pipeline is now 10 years old. In April 2016, the state denied the water permit. Courts upheld it. The company tried again in 2025, then withdrew in November after three notices that its application was incomplete. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION What's the solution? Approve pipeline projects with capacity that bring in domestic gas. Keep reliable power plants running until real replacements are built and tested. Approve the construction of new refineries. Be honest about what climate mandates cost and phase them in at a pace working families can afford. Judge success by lower bills and steady supply, not ribbon-cuttings. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP And most importantly: Vote for candidates this November who are dedicated to American energy independence, supporting sensible and robust expansion of both production and refinement of our own bountiful energy supply.

articles.title: Ultimátum a los jugadores de LIV Golf
articles.standfirst: El DP World Tour no permitirá que se compaginen sus torneos con los de LIV Golf 2.0
articles.summary: El DP World Tour no permitirá que se compaginen sus torneos con los de LIV Golf 2.0
articles.body: LIV Golf 2.0 todavía no ha nacido y no sabemos ni tan siquiera si verá la luz pese a los 300 millones de dólares que está dispuesta a invertir la financiera BC Partners. El motivo no es otro que la cantidad de dificultades que va a tener para que haya jugadores que continúen ligados al proyecto. La nueva versión de la superliga tiene previsto un calendario de 10 torneos, cinco de ellos en Estados Unidos. Hasta aquí todo bien, pero existe un gran problema: la temporada de cualquier jugador se compone de al menos 25 torneos, por lo que para llegar a este número sería necesario competir en otro/s circuito/s. Por supuesto, el PGA Tour (circuito estadounidense) no está dispuesto a abrir la mano y el DP World Tour tampoco lo va a hacer, según ha declarado su director ejecutivo a la BBC. El caso es que este año el DPWT acordó con algunos de sus miembros que también jugaban en la superliga, que no los sancionaría a cambio de acudir a determinados torneos. Pues bien, dicha ‘bula’ ya no se va a prorrogar en 2027. "Los jugadores tienen que tomar una decisión", declaró Guy Kinnings, CEO del DP World Tour, a BBC Sport. "Tenemos normas y reglamentos que existen para proteger nuestro circuito y que todos nuestros miembros deben cumplir. Los jugadores que no estén dispuestos a cumplir con nuestras reglas y regulaciones no deberían intentar unirse a nuestro circuito". Queda claro que el DPWT ya no aceptará a jugadores del LIV; se terminó ese intento de coexistir que sólo ha durado un año. Es la puntilla para LIV Golf 2.0, pues habrá muchos jugadores que descarten unirse a un circuito de solo 10 eventos y cuya membresía conlleva demasiados perjuicios. Ya sabemos que Jon Rahm ha descartado unirse a LIV 2.0 y que su futuro está en el DP World Tour a menos que alcance algún acuerdo con el PGA Tour. Sergio García ya se desligó de LIV y tiene muy claro que su lugar es regresar el Circuito Europeo para intentar jugar la Ryder Cup. David Puig tiene estatus para jugar el año que viene en el DPWT y ya ha dicho que tampoco seguirá en LIV. Hay jugadores que pertenecen al Circuito Europeo como Tyrrell Hatton, Victor Perez o Tom McKibbin que aún se deben pronunciar pero, por ejemplo, Joaquín Niemann está ahora en tierra de nadie. En el caso de Josele Ballester, puede competir en el Asian Tour porque ya ganó allí, pero está intentado acceder al DPWT a través de la escuela. Una de las grandes incógnitas es que será de Phil Mickelson, que este año sólo jugó el LIV Golf Sudáfrica en marzo, y por tanto en esas fechas el año que viene podría estar ya en el Champions Tour (circuito de veteranos del PGA Tour).

articles.summary: Screencaps, America's Best Daily Column, tackles Landry Kiffin wearing UT colors at the Red River Shootout while her dad's LSU season spiraled.
articles.body: Welcome to Screencaps, "America's Best Daily Column," as named by the readers. Screencaps, which publishes seven-days-a-week, is a mix of sports, pop culture, and emails from sane readers from around the world. This column isn't for the coastal elites. Give us a week to steal your heart. Our track record is pretty good. Let's have some fun. Landry Kiffin is the poster child for the SEC fans who were known to chant "SEC, SEC, SEC" before NIL evened the playing field PICK A TEAM! While her dad's season was spiraling out of control Saturday night in Lexington, Kentucky, Landry was in Texas rooting for the No. 1 team in the nation in the Red River Shootout. "U win some u lose some," Landry wrote on TikTok when questioned about her ability to pick a winning team in the SEC. In another video, Landry added, "And go Tigers. We'll be watching at a bar when that game starts." UNRANKED OKLAHOMA KNOCKS OFF NO. 1 TEXAS IN WALK-OFF FASHION AFTER ARCH MANNING'S ROUGH 4TH QUARTER Why go to a UT game and wear UT colors when your dad has to play this team on Nov. 14? "Spying," she wrote. Imagine Nick Saban's daughter openly rooting for a rival SEC program back in like 2010 while her father was in the middle of absolute wars to win the league. This is where we're at with this TikTok generation. Just like the players and coaches in the NIL era, the influencer daughters aren't loyal either. Even the biggest of you SEC homers know that LSU shouldn't be getting this sort of respect. Random emails on a Monday morning – Lee D. in Tampa writes: Good genes. Kinsey: Based on my research, I don't believe there's ever been a mother-daughter sideline reporting tandem to work an NFL game. If we go even further, the NFL, to my knowledge, has never had a mother-daughter-daughter sideline reporting TRIO. Melissa's daughters are twins. One goes to Auburn and the other goes to Stanford. NFL QB & CHEERLEADER SISTER BELIEVED TO BE LEAGUE'S FIRST SIBLING DUO, BOAT RAMP FIGHT & EDDIE GEORGE'S HOUSE Will they go into the family business? Stay tuned. – Greg in Nebraska checks in: I read Screencaps Thursday and saw what you had written about signs in yards changing opinions. When I read it I was definitely a no. That would never impact my vote. Friday morning I was taking my daughter to school and saw a sign for a candidate that I know and was going to vote for in the yard a of a lefty house and now I’m a yes it will change my mind. The guy I thought I was voting for is the dad of a guy I worked with a few years ago. Met the dad a couple of times and he was a good guy so I was ok with voting for him. After I looked up what he supports, I’m voting for the other guy. I’m glad the lefty house had his sign or i would never have looked him up and would have voted for the wrong guy. – Gen X. Warren in Florida has a message for the Dolphins: Congrats to the Bengals on their W. I hope someone in the Ross family, owners of the Miami Dolphins, sees this. SELL THE TEAM! No one trusts you to make good decisions. No coach wants to work for you, no matter the money, because it’s such a toxic environment. But you’re making too much money to care (stadium). Sell the team to an owner who cares, and save the legacy! Us fans need to demand more, per Armando last year. I’d say we’ll protest, but Mrs. Gen X Warren M. is a Lions fan, so we’re going to Lions at Miami game next month… – Susan G. says: I truly believe the Dallas Cowboys will not be a winning team again until Jerry passes away and they replace Dak. I know I know he has a great pass completion percentage but he can’t do it when it counts. I am 67 years old and I have been a Cowboys fan since I can remember, but these days I don’t expect them to win. It is really sad! Golf integrity is one of the biggest issues of our lives right now How do I know? Wait until you see how many emails this topic generated over the weekend. Normally, I'll get maybe six emails on a hot topic over a weekend because you guys have lives to live. This weekend, it was completely different. We have ourselves a hot topic. – Kevin W. emails: I love the question about golf integrity. I belong to a private club, and it's a constant debate. We like other clubs have a "men's day" where all the tee times that day put money into a pot and play various games. This is where the convenience of technology created an issue. We, like yourself, and lots of other golf clubs, started using Golf Genius. Nice and convenient to enter scores; HOWEVER, it also posts scores as they are happening. So, what happens when the guys who go off early post a good score? The late guys see the number they have to beat and BINGO, suddenly 5-footers are good, and those groups are winning everything. Our club's first solution to the problem was to buy a very expensive software called CAP patrol from a bunch of data scientists. Basically, it was the socialist version of golf handicaps that punished good golfers to even out the field for the higher handicappers. It would cherry-pick low rounds and say you're better than your index and you MUST BE cheating otherwise. There were a ton of other factors, and nobody understood the algorithm of who got capped and who didn't, and the company wouldn't disclose it. It's very popular with private clubs on the east and west coasts. We quickly scrapped it. The simple solution this year was to go old school and stop the live scoreboard. Pretty much fixed the issue. In general, if you want to fix giving short putts, always have a money game going. My group of guys rarely, if ever, just go out and play a round just to play. We always have some dollars on the line; even if it's just a few bucks, it keeps the integrity there, as a short putt can change a game quickly. Just my $.02 – Rural MN Dave agrees: I played in a group for many years that played strict rules of golf and no gimmes. One of the group members was playing on a 9 handicap but was really closer to a 6. The strength of his game was chipping and putting. One day he had an 18 inch birdie putt with several skins carryovers riding on it. He stepped up to the putt, taking his time and doing his regular routine, and cold yanked it, never even touched the hole. He looked up, red-faced, and said "and that's why we don't do gimmes!" – Michael in Bossier City, Louisiana says: Your recent article on shaving golf scores did not shock me the least bit. I believe that gimmie putts really skew one’s score when playing the same course conditions. However, not all course conditions are equal. Do you play on a goat ranch city course or a private near PGA standards. I would love to witness a professional golfer score scratch or better on the city course I play regularly; bare fairways and tree roots jutting out in all directions. Rolling the ball slightly to find that last remaining few blades of grass in the fairways or safety setting away from tree roots that are three inches exposed to the surface becomes a must for sanity; you are still accountable to that next golf shot. Now, I’ve played in regional and state tournaments that would white mark a tenth of my course as no play areas because of root or extreme bare spot areas. Then again, I’m not disagreeing with you on most of your points of play. If you are behind a tree or in the rough, then you need to hit your best way out and onto the green to putt it out. More to note! I’m a 6.8 handicap in which I play a fairly nice city course other than the tree root issues and played Robert Trent courses resulting in a near score equivalence. articles.title: DP World Tour bans LIV Golf players, ending Ryder Cup eligibility
articles.summary: The DP World Tour is banning LIV Golf members from competing in its events starting in 2027, another blow to LIV Golf's future.
articles.body:
The DP World Tour is banning LIV Golf members from competing in its events starting in 2027.

Unlike the PGA Tour—which had suspended LIV players since LIV launched in 2022—the DP World Tour had been granting LIV players conditional releases to participate in tournaments. It was a move that was partially done in order to keep several LIV individuals eligible for the Ryder Cup, as the DP World Tour overseas the European team. That included a settlement earlier this year with Tyrrell Hatton and (after a prolonged public fight) Jon Rahm paying outstanding fines for defecting to the former Saudi league. RELATED: Jon Rahm's LIV Golf gamble is over and nobody won

However, those still with LIV must apply for DP World Tour membership by Nov. 16, and guidelines now stipulate that double-dipping between tours is not allowed. More than a dozen LIV players had status on both tours, including Rahm, Hatton and Tom McKibbin.

In a statement to the BBC, DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings said, "Players need to make a choice. We have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by. Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour."

In August, LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil asserted LIV wanted to "complete, not compete" the golf ecosystem, a comment that upset DP World Tour officials after LIV tried to poach several DP World Tour tournaments and sponsors. Additionally, O'Neil accused a DP World Tour leader of contacting LIV players to discuss their options; subsequent reporting indicated it was actually player agents contacting the DP World Tour.

Last week Rahm's attorneys told a New Jersey bankruptcy court that Rahm does not want to be part of LIV's future. Hatton, who has made four Ryder Cup appearances for Team Europe, has not made his intentions public.

Aside from Rahm, Sergio Garcia was granted an exit from his contract and fellow Spaniard David Puig said he was no longer interested in playing with LIV. Attorneys for Cam Smith, Matt Wolff and others asked the court whether Garcia's request sets a precedent for their clients.

Also last week, LIV's new investor, BC Partners, extended the deadline for players to sign up for the league to Oct. 25. "We're super committed," BC Partners CEO Ted Goldthorpe said at a London conference. "As [LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil] said, we're going to start hiring back employees and planning for next year's events. All systems go.

"The next 22 days will be about signing up the players, and I feel very good about that. We've had a lot of constructive dialogue with them. We obviously have a deadline now, but that's the next big step for us."

However, there are questions if BC Partners is truly interested in running the league, as it has a history of taking on trouble companies for future tax credits. The next bankruptcy hearing is scheduled for this Wednesday.

articles.title: Michael Brennan is officially a dude, Blades Brown is coming and time is Jon Rahm's best friend
articles.summary: Michael Brennan's third PGA Tour win at the Baycurrent Classic vaults him to world No. 20 in what's been a quiet yet meteoric rise for the star.
articles.body: The PGA Tour has always had the great problem of having so much young talent that many up-and-comers fall through the cracks and don't get the attention they deserve until they quietly put together a resume that suddenly smacks you in the face. Nobody on Tour right now may optimize that more than Michael Brennan. On the topic of young talent, Blades Brown is headed to the PGA Tour next year. At just 19 years old and some change, he's the youngest player ever to earn his Tour card through the Korn Ferry Tour after finishing ninth on the season-long points list. In other news, LIV Golf suffered a haymaker amid its bankruptcy mess, with Jon Rahm officially opting to split with the league as its future remains entirely up in the air. While it's so easy to look at the (many) negatives involving Rahm and his run with LIV, there is a very obvious yet important reality to look forward to. Welcome to Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you should know. Be sure to follow Mark on X @itismarkharris or email him at mark.harris@outkick.com. Michael Brennan deserves your respect When you think of young stars on Tour, let's call it guys who are 26 or younger, the likes of Jackson Koivun (21), Akshay Bhatia (24), Tom Kim (24), Michael Thorbjornsen (25), Jacob Bridgeman (26), and Ludvig Aberg (26) immediately come to mind, and rightfully so. After what 24-year-old Michael Brennan accomplished in Japan over the weekend, his name firmly belongs in that group. The Baycurrent Classic marked Brennan's 33rd career start on the PGA Tour, and after beginning Sunday's final round tied for the lead, he went out and posted a 3-under 68 to earn a one-shot victory, giving him three career wins, all coming in under 12 months' time. Brennan's maiden win came at the 2025 Bank of Utah Championship in November against an admittedly weaker field. His second trip to the winner's circle, a three-shot victory, came this August at the Wyndham Championship against a stronger crop of players fighting for a spot into the FedEx Cup Playoffs. While the Wyndham could be described as his first "big boy" win, his victory at the Baycurrent, on international soil, is the most impressive of the three, as he held off the likes of Xander Schauffele, Brian Harman, Ryan Gerard, Keith Mitchell, and Bridgeman en route to victory. Brennan was ranked 61st in the world in late July, but has catapulted himself all the way to No. 20 in what can only be described as a quiet, yet meteoric rise. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The former Wake Forest star turned professional in 2024, made quick work of the PGA Tour Americas circuit in 2025 with three wins to earn a spot on the Korn Ferry Tour in 2026, but ultimately skipped that step. His start in the 2025 Bank of Utah Championship came via a sponsor's exemption, and he went out and won the event, his first career start on Tour as a pro, by four shots. So, about a year into his professional career, Brennan had already earned a PGA Tour membership, and less than a year on from that maiden victory, he's earned two more wins. He also made the cut in all four major championships in 2026, which is something only 13 other players can say they accomplished. The Virginia native has proven he knows how to do the hardest part – actually win – and also happens to rank second and third, respectively, in average club head speed and driving distance on Tour. Brennan is one of the best young players on the planet, period. Blades Brown keeps meeting huge expectations It's safe to say Blades Brown made the right call skipping out on that whole college experience thing. Since before he could drive a car, which admittedly wasn't all that long ago, the expectation for Blades Brown has simply been 'the next guy.' While he hasn't won a professional event at this point in his insanely young career, he's just about met every expectation out there. It has been a steady climb for the Nashville native since he made his professional debut in January 2025 at 17 years old at The American Express. He's made the most out of countless sponsors' exemptions on the PGA Tour and put together an incredibly consistent campaign on the Korn Ferry Tour in 2026 with six Top 10s and just two missed cuts in 18 starts, which was plenty to earn a spot on Tour in 2027. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE When the calendar flips in January, things get as real as possible for a guy who doesn't turn 20 until May, but Brown has shown absolutely no reason to doubt him as he's been Mr. Consistent. In 11 starts on Tour in 2026, Brown missed just two cuts, finished solo third at the Puerto Rico Open, and picked up a total of seven Top 25 finishes. His career is very simply on the exact, consistent trajectory many expected it to be on at this point. Currently ranked 97th in the world, it will be fascinating to see how Brown plays out of the gates in 2027. Sneaking inside the Top 50 and earning a Masters invite would be quite the story. We'll eventually not care about Jon Rahm's stint on LIV It's so easy to say that Jon Rahm made a mistake when he left the PGA Tour for LIV Golf in 2024. You could claim it was a decision made out of greed, as he made the move for hundreds of millions of dollars. Then again, 99.9% of humanity would leave one job for another to acquire generational wealth, plus, Rahm was up front that money was the major factor behind his decision to join the then Saudi-backed circuit. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER You could also claim that the move hurt his reputation. He made the jump at just 30 years old in the prime of his career with two major championships already in his back pocket. While it's fair to focus on those aspects now, our now will soon become our then, and Rahm has an ample amount of time to make his brief career on LIV Golf seem like a forgettable blip on his resume. While at this point in time we don't know how he'll do it, the Spaniard will get back to competing on the PGA Tour against the best players in the world on a consistent basis. Maybe we see that in six months, maybe it takes 18 months, who knows, but when it happens, it'll be a jolt to the PGA Tour from every angle. Yes, two decades from now, golf fans will make jokes about Rahm leaving for LIV Golf for a couple of years while remembering him making the announcement in a ridiculous letterman jacket, but our level of caring about it at that point, in the grand scheme of things, won't even exist.

articles.title: 'Validation and relief' for Forrest after Spanish Open win
articles.summary: Grant Forrest on dealing with last hole nerves in Madrid and the euphoria of the biggest win of his career.
articles.body:
"I don't think I've ever been as nervous on a golf course."

Scotland's Grant Forrest knocked in a last-hole birdie at the Spanish Open on Sunday to seal the biggest win of his career.

Along with the £480,000 first prize come places at the Masters and The Open next year.

It has also propelled the 33-year-old up 156 places the world rankings to 140th.

Playing partner Victor Perez missed his chance to overtake clubhouse leader Eugenio Chacarra, leaving the door open for Forrest to claim his third DP World Tour title and a first professional win outside Scotland.

"When the stage was set for me to try and hole the winning putt, my hands were shaking," he told BBC Scotland.

"I don't know how I managed to make it go in. Delighted that it did, obviously.

"You just fall back into your routine. Breathing has been a huge part of what I've worked on recently - and that really helped throughout the whole day."

Forrest earns major invites with Spanish Open win

DP World Tour to refuse LIV players in 2027 season

Forrest has not had much sleep over "a surreal 24 hours" as he flew from Madrid to New Dehli for the DP World India Championship.

Having made his professional bow over a decade ago, he said the victory brought "a lot of validation, relief as well."

On the prospect of a Masters debut in April, he explained: "I was there as a spectator in 2019 and it's just an incredibly special place.

"To have the opportunity to play hasn't sunk in yet."

Forrest has had experience of The Open in 2013 and 2018, at Muirfield and Carnoustie respectively.

"Playing a third at St Andrews is going to be incredible," he added.

Forrest graduated from the European Challenge Tour to the DP World Tour at the end of the 2018 season along with compatriots Robert MacIntyre and David Law.

Connor Syme and Scott Jamieson have won titles in the past two years, along with Ryder Cup star MacIntyre.

"It gives you positive energy when one guy succeeds," Forrest said on the current strength of Scottish golf.

"You know they are not much different in terms of ability, it's just reminding yourself that a win can be round the corner at any point."

articles.title: Bears get optimistic news on Caleb Williams amid potential Week 6 return
articles.summary: This Caleb Williams update is a very encouraging sign for Week 6.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears lost Caleb Williams near the end of Week 2 in their loss to the Minnesota Vikings , and the combination of Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent has gone 2-1 since then.

But after a rough Week 5 against the NFC North rival Green Bay Packers , the Bears are in desperate need of Williams back on the field. Fortunately, the latest update is some good news for such a future coming to pass.

According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network , the Bears' QB is trending in the right direction, and that "all signs" are pointing towards Williams returning to the Bears' offense this upcoming Week 6 matchup.

Bears get good Caleb Williams news for Week 6 playing odds

"The fact that Caleb Williams was working out before the game, in a pretty strenuous workout... this is a very good sign," Rapoport said. "... All signs point to Caleb Williams being back on the field for Chicago..."

With a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons on tap, the Bears getting Williams back would be huge. After missing three weeks, he's one week away from missing the equivalent amount of time as if he were placed on injured reserve.

Returning for Week 6 against the Falcons would prove the Bears were right not to place Williams on IR. They shouldn't rush Williams back, but they really need him back after the performance from the Packers QBs in Week 5.

Fortunately, this update from Rapoport points to the Bears' franchise quarterback being back in action for Week 6 against the Falcons.

Nothing is confirmed just yet, and he'll need to suit up during practice this week to prove he's good to go. But based on his pre-game workout and this report, Williams is clearly trending in the right direction.

The 3-2 Bears are tied for last place in the NFC North with the Packers and Detroit Lions , sitting 2.0 games back of the 5-0 Minnesota Vikings.

If the Bears want any chance of winning the division again, they're going to need to get Williams back as soon as possible. That looks possible, if not likely, as Williams returning to the field for Week 6 is very much in play.

articles.title: El imparable ascenso de Eugenio Chacarra
articles.standfirst: Acaba de entrar por primera vez en el 'top 50' mundial. En el DP World Tour sólo Patrick Reed lo supera. Aspira a convertirse en el tercer español que gana la Orden de Mérito
articles.summary: Acaba de entrar por primera vez en el 'top 50' mundial. En el DP World Tour sólo Patrick Reed lo supera. Aspira a convertirse en el tercer español que gana la Orden de Mérito
articles.body: Eugenio López-Chacarra (Madrid, 26 años) encadena dos torneos en los que se ha confirmado como uno de los jugadores más espectaculares a los que se puede ver en un campo de golf. Que el madrileño esté peleando por ganar en el DP World Tour no es casualidad, y él lleva tiempo avisándolo. Su frase “jugando bien soy uno de los mejores del mundo” cada vez cobra más sentido. Este año lleva dos victorias: en el KLM Open (Países Bajos) y el Open de Italia, dos abiertos nacionales de abolengo en el Circuito Europeo. En Italia cerró el torneo con una tarjeta de 64 golpes y a esto hay que sumar su empuje al inicio de las rondas finales del Open de Francia, donde arrancó con cuatro birdies en sus seis primeros hoyos, y del Open de España, donde descontó cinco golpes al líder en los primeros nueve hoyos; en el European Masters también atacó el domingo y tiró 67 golpes para terminar cuarto. Un jugador que con tanta frecuencia demuestra su capacidad para afrontar remontadas los domingos no aparece todos los días. Sin duda, Chacarra –los circuitos y rankings han eliminado el López de su apellido compuesto- es el tipo de golfista que engancha al aficionado y pone emoción a los domingos; de los que sale a ganar y apunta siempre a la bandera aunque a veces salga cruz. “Yo sabía que necesitaba hacer ruido desde el principio y muchos otros iban a sufrir. Cuando mi nombre está arriba, a mucha gente le cuesta”, afirmó tras certificar su segundo puesto en el Open de España. Este curso son ya seis los ‘top 5’ los que acumula y ocho los ‘top 10’ totales. Eugenio, que ha ganado torneos en LIV Golf, DP World Tour y Asian Tour, ha demostrado ser un gran competidor. Su enorme temporada lo ha llevado de momento hasta el puesto 50 del ranking mundial de golf; es decir, a día de hoy tendría plaza para jugar los cuatro Majors y hay que tener en cuenta que los torneos del DP World Tour entregan menos puntos que los del PGA Tour. En su caso, sólo ha jugado un Major, el British Open, en el que fue 46º; también disputó un torneo del PGA Tour, el Puerto Rico Open, en el que finalizó 21º. Chacarra es a día de hoy el jugador cuyo circuito principal es el DP World Tour con segundo mejor ranking mundial tras Patrick Reed (30º), pero en el caso de este último disputó los cuatro grandes. En la Race to Dubai, la clasificación anual del DPWT, ya es segundo con 3.257 puntos, solo por detrás del estadounidense Patrick Reed (3.423) y por delante de Rory McIlroy (3.115). “Lo que importa son los últimos cuatro torneos”, apuntó Eugenio tras acabar en Madrid. Esta semana, aún con su dedo del pie derecho roto, estará en India; justo después vendrá Corea y después serán las finales en Abu Dabi y Dubai. Chacarra está en plena pelea por la otrora conocida como Orden de Mérito, un galardón que en España sólo han ganado Severiano Ballesteros y Jon Rahm.

articles.title: Jon Rahm ya tiene fecha para reaparecer
articles.standfirst: El 'León de Barrika' jugará el Abu Dhabi Championship en noviembre
articles.summary: El 'León de Barrika' jugará el Abu Dhabi Championship en noviembre
articles.body: Jon Rahm ya sabe en qué torneo reaparecerá tras haberse visto obligado a renunciar a su participación en el Open de España debido a su inminente paternidad. El ‘León de Barrika’ no quería faltar a la cita en el Club de Campo, más aún porque se había comprometido con el DP World Tour a jugar un número determinado de torneos de este circuito en la presente temporada, pero las circunstancias mandan. El caso es que ya no se trata sólo de cumplir con el DPWT. Fallar el corte en el BMW PGA Championship hace unas semanas y no poder venir al Open de España ha hecho que no sume puntos de cara a la Race to Dubai, la clasificación anual del DPWT. Actualmente ocupa el puesto 46 y la final de Dubái sólo la disputan los 50 mejores de ese ranking. El circuito cierra la temporada con los eventos de Abu Dabi y Dubái, denominados como finales o ‘DP World Tour Play-Offs’, siendo además los que más puntos otorgan con diferencia (9.000 y 12.000). El Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship sólo lo juegan los 70 mejores y ‘Rahmbo’ está obligado cuanto menos a disputarlo si quiere asegurarse un puesto en la final (DP World Tour Championship). Por lo tanto, la reaparición de Jon Rahm tras saberse que no tiene intención de seguir en LIV Golf el año que viene sucederá en el citado Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship (5-8 de noviembre), un torneo que nunca había jugado; si todo le va bien, la semana siguiente estaría en Dubái. El vasco se unirá en Abu Dabi a jugadores como el campeón del torneo, Aaron Rai; el vigente campeón de la Race to Dubai, Rory McIlroy; o los primeros clasificados este año, Patrick Reed y Eugenio Chacarra.

articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. One minute, you're firing up the grill for Labor Day, and the next you're trying to explain to your kids that we can't carve pumpkins yet because it's still 85 degrees in Florida and they'll rot before sundown tomorrow. Anyway, it's just funny to me. We do this every year. You really wanna go down a wormhole? Go look up what different states call this day. In Hawaii, for example, it's referred to as "Discoverers' Day." It's all silly to me. The gaslighting. The pandering. The nonsense. It's not that serious, folks. Lighten up. Can we all please just be normal again? And that's your Columbus Day Ted Talk. You are welcome! OK, let's hop in our own boats and head east to check in on LPGA star, Charley Hull, who took the weekend off to enjoy some R&R with the ladies: COMEDIAN TIM DILLON SLAMS SYDNEY SWEENEY CRITICS UPSET WITH STEAMY AD: 'HOW INSANE IS THAT? ' Sydney Sweeney has a response for the outrage brigade! Once again, Charley Hull doesn't miss. What a content run out of the best LPGA golfer on the planet right now. What a heater. "The amount of backlash that [it] is getting, I just don't understand the way people's brains work," the world’s 8th-ranked female golfer said of the ridiculous reactions from other female athletes who completely overreacted. "They're making a big deal out of nothing. It's an actress slash model modeling for an advert. And I think she owns the company as well," Hull added. Patriot. articles.title: Columbia local Ross Steelman wins Korn Ferry Tour season-long points race
articles.summary: Former Rock Bridge and Mizzou golfer Ross Steelman won the Korn Ferry Tour season-long points race, earning his PGA Tour card and a spot in two of golf's mos...
articles.body:
You can find Columbia's Ross Steelman at Pebble Beach, TPC Sawgrass and at a PGA Tour stop near you in 2027.

Steelman, a former Rock Bridge High and Missouri men's golf player, secured the season-long points list title on the Korn Ferry Tour on Sunday. By winning the yearlong points race, Steelman earned a spot in both the 2027 U.S. Open and the 2027 PLAYERS Championship.

The Columbia local moved ahead of Scotland's Sandy Scott in the final week of the season with a tied-for-12th finish at the Korn Ferry Tour Championship, which was played Thursday through Sunday in Virginia. Scott finished tied for 43rd, giving Steelman enough points to climb back into first place in the season-long standings.

The top 20 players on the Korn Ferry Tour points list earned PGA Tour cards. Steelman had already secured his PGA Tour status earlier this year.

Finishing No. 1, however, comes with extra benefits.

The U.S. Open, one of golf's four major championships, will take place at the iconic Pebble Beach Golf Links from June 17-20 in California. As it stands, that will be Steelman's first major championship appearance.

The PLAYERS Championship, which is the marquee event on the PGA Tour schedule, will be played at TPC Sawgrass in March in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida.

Steelman won twice this year on the KFT, taking home the trophy at the The Blue Championship in July in Colorado and at the Albertsons Boise Open in August in Idaho. Those were his first victories since turning professional in 2023.

He will have full status on the PGA Tour in 2027.

Steelman spent three seasons at Mizzou between 2018-21. He won two collegiate events, including Missouri's home tournament at The Club at Old Hawthorne in 2021. Steelman transferred to Georgia Tech for his final two years of college and was a first-team All-American in 2023.

While at Rock Bridge, Steelman won the MSHSAA Class 4 individual title in 2018, also helping the Bruins to the team championship.

Steelman is currently ranked No. 74 in the Official World Golf Rankings.

Fellow former Missouri golfer Hayden Buckley finished 65th in the season-long race, missing out on a berth to the Korn Ferry Tour Championship. Buckley retained conditional status for the Korn Ferry Tour next season.

Two former Mizzou golfers — Charlie Crockett and Jack Lundin — are competing for Korn Ferry Tour cards this coming weekend at the PGA Tour Americas Tour Championship.

Crockett and Lundin currently sit sixth and seventh, respectively, the tour's season-long race. They need to finish in the top-10 to earn a Korn Ferry Tour card.

articles.title: Kerr ‘leaning toward' small-ball Warriors lineup to open season with Porzingis absent
articles.summary: Draymond Green will be battling opposing centers for Golden State and Gui Santos may start in the Warriors' new-look lineup with Kristaps Porzingis not expec...
articles.body:
Blink twice if you've heard this before: The Golden State Warriors are going small. Small , though, brings a bit more heft this fall than in years past.

After a couple preseason games starting Draymond Green at center, head coach Steve Kerr said Monday he's "leaning toward" a starting five of Stephen Curry , Brandin Podziemski , Gui Santos , Yaxel Lendeborg and Green to kick off the regular season Oct. 21 against the Lakers. Small-ball is back, as the three-man frontcourt of Santos, Lendeborg and Green has flashed notable offensive synergy this October, bringing a heap of connective playmaking that has often pried open the paint for back-cuts from Podziemski and rookie Lendeborg.

"It's a little different look than having a traditional big," Kerr said, after the Warriors' preseason win over Sacramento Saturday. "So, I like it. But it's just - we've only played it a handful of minutes."

They'll play it plenty more, now, out of sheer necessity. Golden State is planning to keep 40-year-old Al Horford to around 20 minutes a game in 2026-27, Kerr said, making it hard to finagle rotations where he's a consistent starter. The Warriors are encouraged by 25-year-old reserve Charles Bassey, but need more evidence that the five-year NBA journeyman can share the floor with Green offensively.

And, of course, there's the ongoing mystery of Kristaps Porzingis and his availability, which should have an answer sooner than later. Kerr said Porzingis will be at Chase Center Tuesday - as the Warriors are in Las Vegas for a preseason game against the Lakers - to meet with Golden State director of performance Rick Celebrini and the rest of the Warriors' medical staff.

That's something. For two weeks, since general manager Mike Dunleavy announced Sept. 28 that Porzingis would be out indefinitely with a health issue, Kerr has appeared in the dark on where Porzingis is and what exactly he's dealing with.

When asked Monday if he knew where Porzingis has been recently - in the Bay Area or out of the country - Kerr declined to comment, citing Porzingis's privacy.

Kerr's admission about the Warriors' likely season-opening starting unit, though, is further evidence that the 31-year-old Porzingis won't be ready to start the season. And perhaps longer.

"All that will be determined once we get him back here, and have discussions, and figure out where he is, all that stuff," Kerr said Monday, asked if Porzingis would be able to play in the regular season.

For now, the Warriors have settled on a five-man combination that could ease the defensive burden on Green with the length of its collective frontcourt. The 6-foot-7 Santos is only picking up importance to this Warriors rotation by the week, and has looked stout defensively guarding wings this preseason. Rookie Lendeborg, meanwhile, has a definite defensive learning curve but has flashed help-side destructiveness, with a 7-foot-3 wingspan .

It's still a tall order, though, to ask the 36-year-old Green to grapple with opposing centers nightly. Kerr's ability to Frankenstein a 48-minute center rotation out of Green, Horford, any active version of Porzingis, Bassey and two-way rookie Graham Ike will be one of the defining challenges of this Warriors season.

Meanwhile, Stephen Curry will ramp up to some second-half action against the Lakers Tuesday after playing minimally throughout this preseason, Kerr said. Horford won't make the trip to Vegas, as part of regularly scheduled maintenance.

The Warriors cut preseason standout Miles Kelly from their training-camp roster Sunday to make room for former Grizzlies forward Tyler Burton. Kelly will head to the G League after Santa Cruz acquired his rights in late September. He could make some noise after shining in a 24-point, six-three performance against the Trail Blazers last week.

The 25-year-old Burton played 12 games last season for Memphis last season, averaging 10.8 points in 25.6 minutes per game. A 6-foot-7 wing, Burton spent four collegiate seasons at Richmond before starting for Villanova in 2023-24.

articles.title: ‘DGC game of chess tougher this year’: Shiv Kapur decodes the lies and breaks at Delhi’s iconic golf course
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Rory McIlroy, superstar draw of the DP World India Championship for the second year running, would probably like a deeper reading of the jungle
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Rory McIlroy, superstar draw of the DP World India Championship for the second year running, would probably like a deeper reading of the jungle book that is the Delhi Golf Club this time round. Perhaps, deep is not the right word here with the bogeyman in the bushes listening.“The next time I hit my driver will be in Abu Dhabi,” the World No. 2 had said after his Pro-Am rehearsal here last year at the inaugural DPWIC. Laughter had ensued on a lazy Wednesday afternoon. And the Masters champ eventually finished T-26th at 11-under before packing his bags on Sunday, with a little regret and a few lessons. But the best thing about golf is that you immediately move on.Two strokes behind Rory was Shiv Kapur that week, as the bestplaced Indian. Kapur has moved on too, from his childhood backyard. The Asian Tour website tells us that once he had great fun shooting a 44-over 166 at an AsiaPacific Juniors event, and for the 44-year-old, the many meanderings on the course over the years had yielded laughter, pain, pressure, and finally an Asian Tour triumph at the Panasonic India in 2017. “Monkey is finally off my back now,” he had said, smiling out of relief then. It was probably the same emotions experienced by McIlroy at Augusta in 2025.Based out of Dubai now, Shiv returns to India to play IGPL events, and work on course projects — the 9-hole golf course in Lonavala opens Nov 22, where every Wednesday, children and people from the local community will be exempt from fees. But the minute he takes the gateway to the green haven amidst the bustle of central Delhi, there is no better place to be.“Somebody of Rory’s or Tommy Fleetwood’s calibre may not struggle but certainly, it’s a very unique week on the Tour because they don’t play too many courses like this. It’s like a game of chess where you have to place it in certain areas,” Shiv talked about why strategy is valued over brute force here. “It is more of a power game these days where people outmuscle courses. But DGC is one of those classic tests where you have to think your way around. It’s a week where most players will probably not have the big stick in the bag.”He doesn’t see a repeat of Fleetwood’s winning score of 22-under. “The rough is around 4 to 5 inches, which is, at par with the US Open. You have to keep it in the short grass. It’s going to be a tougher test.”More from ShivTougher after the Gary Player redesign: After the Gary Player redesign of the Lodhi course, it’s a bit more strategic. Earlier, the greens were fairly flat, so you got a lot of birdie opportunities. The main changes were the bunkering and the contouring of the greens. The greens have a lot more slope, more pin positions. There are certain pins this week that you won’t be able to go at. With a combination of high rough and having these sections of the greens, it will be difficult on some holes. Pin placements dictate the entire strategy on hole 7 (par-3) and the 9th (par-4). On the 18th, the front section of the green is very, very narrow, so you have about a five-yard entrance to enter.The final ‘Augusta’ stretch: The real challenge comes when you stand on the 14th tee. You have two par-5s, which are both risk reward par-fives 14 and 18. You have a short par-4 No. 15 and a par-3 with a deep bunker on 17. You can end up playing the last five holes, 3- or 4-underpar or 3- or 4-over. In terms of comparison, I think Augusta National is a bit like that where the 13th is a par 5, the 15th is a par 5. So you see a lot of eagles, bogeys, double bogeys. You can see wild swings on the leaderboard.On IGPL players in the field: The idea is not about calling it PGTI vs IGPL. articles.summary: LUCKNOW: A post-mortem report of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma, who died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment near
articles.body: LUCKNOW: A post-mortem report of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma, who died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment near Balu Adda on October 9, records 11 entries detailing external injuries and six broad categories of internal findings.The report notes tears in both lungs, injuries to the liver and spleen, substantial internal bleeding and a fracture of the right pelvic bone. Doctors attributed his death to shock and haemorrhage resulting from the injuries.Police are investigating whether Sharma jumped, was pushed or fell accidentally. Investigators are examining CCTV footage, witness statements and physical evidence from the scene to reconstruct the sequence of events.They are also considering a crime scene recreation to establish the likely point of impact and determine whether the evidence at the site is consistent with the injuries recorded in the autopsy. Officials said the post-mortem findings alone do not establish how Sharma went over the edge.Mother accuses girlfriend, others of assault and murderSharma’s mother, Ranjana Sharma, has accused his girlfriend, model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey, a driver, an associate identified as Adil, and others of assaulting and murdering her son.Hazratganj police have registered an FIR based on her complaint. The allegations have not yet been established.Ranjana told police that she received a call from Adil around 7pm on October 9, informing her that Sharma’s condition had worsened and that he was being taken to King George’s Medical University (KGMU).She alleged that when the family reached the hospital, the people who had accompanied Sharma showed him to them from a distance before fleeing. Doctors subsequently declared him dead, according to her complaint.Ranjana also alleged that Dubey had harassed Sharma for months, threatened to implicate him in false cases and damage his reputation, and used blackmail and violence to pressure him into continuing the relationship.Police have yet to establish these allegations.Police search for people linked to caseAssistant commissioner of police (Hazratganj) Rajneesh Verma said further action would depend on the evidence gathered during the investigation.Police teams have conducted searches in Rae Bareli and Sitapur to trace people linked to the case, he said.Investigators are continuing to examine the medical findings alongside other evidence to establish the circumstances surrounding Sharma’s death.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: City of London gas leak sees about 5,000 evacuated from buildings
articles.summary: A cordon between Threadneedle Street and London Wall has been lifted and people are being allowed back into affected properties.
articles.body:
About 4,700 people were evacuated in the City of London after a gas leak.

The London Fire Brigade (LFB) said it was called to Old Broad Street at 10:55 BST, where crews found a ruptured six-inch gas main at a six-storey office building.

A 200m cordon was put in place between Threadneedle Street and London Wall, with nearby buildings evacuated as a precaution. The brigade has now removed its cordon, and people are being allowed back into affected properties.

A Cadent spokesperson said the pipe was "severely damaged by a private construction team" and stressed the work that caused the damage "had nothing to do with Cadent or its pipework".

Cadent is keeping a road closure in place on Great Winchester Street while engineers complete repairs to the damaged gas pipeline.

Two fire engines from Dowgate and Shadwell fire stations, along with a fire rescue unit from Bethnal Green, attended the incident.

I'm talking the early days of Twitter. It helped build the account, there's no doubt about that. That feels like a lifetime ago. That's how long Amy has been sitting in this exact seat. Readers are still fired up over full integrity golf – Paul in La Crosse, WI shares how his group plays: First, some background. I've been in a golf league 20 years. The league was originally a church mens club league and has been active 52 years. It is no longer church men's club exclusive (they accepted me!). We play Tuesday afternoons at a small 32 par executive course. This is only the 2nd course the league has ever played on. The original, Hillview Golf Course, was a little par 27 course created on farm pasture. Thousands of kids learned to golf there. As some leagues go, we have hole prizes, side games and some non-standard golf rules. To keep the flow moving on the course (we play one group after another) gimmee's on putts were allowed but can only be offered by your playing partner that day. Some players started taking advantage and would assume the gimmee. A couple years ago, in another effort to "keep it movin", the gimmee rule changed to putter length. Hardly any of us are that good/consistant (50+ people in the league). Players have been complaining. Putter lengths obviously differ and matches could be won/lost. So, for next years golf season, the rule has reverted to playing partner gimmee only. – John in Murfreesboro, TN emails: I don't really have a full integrity golf story, but I will say I don't take gimmes unless they're inside 1 foot. Even then, I'll putt most of them, unless we're trying to keep pace. Hole out, that's how I was taught. But it is amazing how quick others are to give you a putt that's not a gimme at all. Having said that, I usually play just to have fun, so sometimes the rules get bent. Being against a tree and in danger of hitting a root? No thanks, move it out. Take an unplayable if you're being completely honest with yourself. In the middle of the fairway but in some idiot's divot? Uh uh. I don't report scores for handicap, never play tournaments, etc., so no one cares what my scorecard reads. I don't even tell my wife when I get home (she doesn't care anyway). I play to enjoy the game and sometimes the rules get in the way of that. I don't usually remember my score anyway, I remember the good shots I hit that day, and try to forget the bad ones! – Jonathan D. makes his Screencaps debut: I have never played 100% "down" because I feel if I m in the middle of the fairway and find a dead spot, I m going to roll in out. Not closer to the hole and not 3 feet away but within 18 inches back or lateral. That being said, the last 2 years I have played all my shots down and whether with my buddies or with my legit handicapped league (my dad's old man group that I play with during the summers), I play them down. It has been some of the most rewarding and frustrating rounds of my life. 50 rounds in just the last 2 summers. I am an elementary school teacher, so most of my golf is summer time. Happily divorced which is the reason I can play so much! I always hovered in the low to mid 80s when I improved my ball position or took mulligan (we often allow 1 on each 9). Over 2 summers, my legit handicap is 13 with some rounds near +18 and others at +8. Last summer I was consistently +18-20. This summer I got it consistently at +10-12. I am not a pro nor do I put in that time. But I take so much more pride in my game now than I ever have before. My dad was a legit scratch (played HS, college and some mini senior tours in his 50s). He is now a +6 (72 years old) and still kicks my ass on the regular. Lol! I'll out drive him by 40 yards and he'll birdie to my bogey. Golf is a special bond that we have. He told me how proud he is that I have gotten my game where it s at. I really don't care what I shoot when we play, as long as we play. Hard to go back to shaving strokes when it's laid out like that...at least for me it is. – Strat says he'll play whatever he wants to play: I play only if the other three guys will play best ball on every shot, on every hole; I always improve my lie; I play a "Mulligan" anywhere, anytime. I play with lots of retired folks and there is no betting. So, almost all folks take multiple mulligans (breakfast balls), move their golf ball around, kick it from behind trees , etc. i don’t mind since we’re not playing for money. However, one incident really pissed me off. On a par 4, i drove the ball well. Then, hit the approach on the green. Long downhill putt. I left myself an 8 foot par putt (uphill) and made the putt.
